root_cause.text: The `dtv5100_i2c_msg()` function in the dtv5100 DVB USB driver fails to validate that the user-controlled `rlen` parameter is within the bounds of the destination buffer `st->data` before performing a `memcpy()` operation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the addition of a bounds check `if (rlen > sizeof(st->data))` immediately preceding the `memcpy(st->data, rbuf, rlen)` call to prevent an out-of-bounds write.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a boundary check on the read length to prevent a buffer overflow in dtv5100_i2c_msg.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check to verify if the read length (rlen) exceeds the size of the destination buffer (st->data) before copying memory.
intent_record.how: Prevents a potential buffer overflow by validating the transfer size and returning an error code (-EINVAL) if it is out of bounds.

candidates.rationale: The memcpy operation copies 'rlen' bytes into 'st->data' without checking if 'rlen' exceeds the size of 'st->data', leading to a buffer overflow.

    [media] dtv5100: don't do DMA on stack
    
    The USB control messages require DMA to work. We cannot pass
    a stack-allocated buffer, as it is not warranted that the
    stack would be into a DMA enabled area.
